we constructed a plasmids containing human α‐Fetprotein promoter/enhancer region and the diphtheria toxing gene fragment A, and that the plasmids could selectively suppress the proliferation of hepatocellular carcinoma cell lines and transplanted tumor in mice.
we developed a plasmid vector, designated as pAF-DTA, that expresses diphtheria fragment A under the control of human AFP promoter/enhancer.

the diphtheria A fragment gene, which is expressed under the control of a human alpha‐fetoprotein promoter, selectively inhibited the growth of hepatoma cells producing AFP, but not of other types of cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel gene therapy system for hepatocellular carcinoma using pAF‐DT‐A.
the selective killing of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cells by using diphtheria toxoid A (DTA) under the control of the promoter/enhancer region of the human AFP gene.
the development of a novel approach for selective inhibition of AFP‐producing tumor cells using pAF‐DTAs.
